Summary
The letter discusses the sender's experience with mail delays and the impact on their writing. The sender mentions the distance from the front line and the changing mail service. They also share personal experiences, such as a sunburn and a movie viewing, and express concern about the death of friends. The sender reflects on their lack of writing and mentions a book they ordered about the U.S. Army in the 1930s. The tone is nostalgic and somewhat melancholic, reflecting on the sender's absence and the passage of time.

--- Page 1 (Beckerman_21a) --- Dear Folk and Ruth, Haven't received mail for about 2 weeks now and it's put a bit of a dampener on my writing. Mail to Australia from the States has fallen off quite a bit. We are pretty far from the front line now. Mail service I guess heads up north to the Philippines. I went to the beach Sunday - it was very hot that day and as usual I got my share of sunburn. Tonight (Monday) went to see the movie "Flame of Barbary Coast" which must of played at home some time ago. Enjoyed all your tidbits in 16 Feb letter about changes around the neighborhood. I had already heard about the death of John Smith and Matthew and the death of [illegible] [illegible] a many more of these to come. Believe it or not our Christmas is - --- Page 2 (Beckerman_21b) --- 2. Packages are still coming in. Received two more the other day. One from a girl at my last leave in New York and another from Chicago. It didn't have a card or return address, but I assume it came from Uncle Max and Katie. I have neglected my mail terribly lately. Until I come I get down and answer a whole pile. I have collecting dust in my drawer. Just haven't felt like writing lately. Really not much to write about. Think it's time for a change for me. It's wonderful to know that you are all well. I'll keep that way until I get back. Which reminds me that I haven't heard from you since I left. --- Page 3 (Beckerman_21c) --- 3. ordered a book the other which tells all about what the U.S. Army have done in this Thirties and plans the have been to. You should be getting it about 3 months after you receive this letter. It's printed in Chicago and is mailed direct. So when you get it - you'll know where it came from. That's about all for tonight. I know I haven't written very often these past few weeks but everything is just as well as ever. Love and regards - and Aunt Sara, Bella, and [illegible] are alive. Good night [illegible]
